analysis:
The PR changes only documentation and a code comment. In docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md it updates the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a description at lines 393-400 of the attention-donation write-budget charging. The description says several blocks are charged as one summed reservation before the first write, falling back to per-block charging when that charge is refused (SSDWriteBehind.chargeWholeDonation). The comment edit in SSDPrefixCache.swift (lines 1081-1083) only qualifies the ordering note. No executable code changes in the supplied evidence, so the diff itself introduces no regression.

Threat context: T-041 covers the SSD prefix cache, including its endurance and write-cap mitigations (the daily write cap, the persistent rolling-day ledger that is not refunded on failure). The documented behavior keeps charges ahead of writes, does not refund them, and fails closed on a corrupt ledger. Blocks skipped after a whole-donation charge stay charged, which is conservative for the cap. No change to TTL, encryption, HMAC tag derivation, DBK3 AAD or scoping is described.

Open integration question: the implementation of SSDWriteBehind.chargeWholeDonation is not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify that the code matches the documented semantics, for example that the summed charge is made before any write, that fallback per-block charging preserves the cap, or that a failed whole-donation charge cannot permit uncharged writes. If that code is part of the same PR, its review is needed. Nothing here shows it is unsafe, and this is a coverage limit rather than a finding.
